HDR scholarships and fees
At UWA, we’re proud to support the next generation of researchers through a range of scholarships funded by the Australian Government, the University and external organisations. These scholarships can help cover tuition fees, living costs, travel, research expenses and relocation.

Higher Degree by Research (HDR) scholarships
Open up a world of opportunities and pursue research in a field that matters to you. At UWA, our HDR scholarships give you the support to dive deeper into what drives you - so you can explore bold ideas, break new ground, and shape real change in your field.

Research Training Program (RTP) scholarships, stipends and allowances
The Australian Government’s Research Training Program (RTP) provides funding to support both domestic and international students undertaking Research Doctorate and Research Master’s degrees. At UWA, RTP funding is used to support eligible students through the following types of scholarships:
Domestic RTP Tuition Fees Offset Scholarships
Automatically provided to all domestic HDR students, without the need for a competitive application process.
International RTP Tuition Fees Offset Scholarships
Awarded to a limited number of international students, via a competitive selection process.
RTP Stipend Scholarships (living allowance)
Awarded to a limited number of domestic and international students, via a competitive selection process. The current value in 2027 is $39,253 per annum.
RTP Allowances
Awarded to assist students with ancillary costs of Higher Degree by Research, such as relocation expenses.

HDR tuition fees
The amount you will pay for tuition fees will depend on your Higher Degree by Research course, your enrolment and your citizenship, as well as any scholarships you may be awarded. Tuition fees are due to be paid at the start of each semester.

HDR scholarships
Explore all research scholarships
UWA offers a range of other prestigious Higher Degree by Research scholarships for outstanding domestic and international applicants who demonstrate exceptional research potential.
We’re committed to access and equity for all students. If you are a prospective researcher who identifies as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, we strongly encourage you to apply for the large number of scholarships available across many disciplines, to help support your research journey.

Find out everything you need to know including eligibility, selection criteria, scholarship conditions and more.
View advice for applicants [PDF 140KB]
Choose your course and supervisor
If you haven’t already, explore your options, select your course or project and reach out to a potential supervisor.
Find out more
Apply for a scholarship
Apply for your chosen course and the 2027 Domestic HDR Scholarship Round as your scholarship selection via the online HDR application portal. This application is for both admission and scholarships. No separate application is required for RTP scholarships consideration.
If you are a current HDR candidate or applicant already holding a UWA HDR Offer Letter, apply for the scholarship via the online Scholarship application form - no additional application is required in HDRhub.
New applicants - HDR Application Portal
Current applicants - HDR Scholarship application form
Fees for domestic HDR students
Citizens of Australia and New Zealand and permanent residents of Australia are exempt from tuition fees if UWA admits them to a HDR course.
This exemption applies for up to four years' full-time equivalent study for a doctorate by research, and two years' full-time equivalent study for a master's by research.
Fees for international HDR students
All international students at UWA must pay tuition fees for their course unless they have a scholarship or sponsorship that covers the fees.
Other fees
All students are required to pay the UWA Student Services and Amenities fee.
This compulsory charge provides access to a range of amenities and services, including recreational, sporting and educational facilities and social, education and representation activities.
